- The best sparse fit I found (free exponents, π/10 forcing) reached about 1.7e-5 NMSE. It still has a sqrt(v)·log(x) term with a free exponent on |v|, so it is not the exact law.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    w=np.pi/10
    p=params[7]; q=params[8]; r=params[9]
    return (params[0] + params[1]*v + params[2]*x + params[3]*x**2
            + params[4]*np.abs(v)**p + params[5]*np.sqrt(v)*np.log(x)
            + params[6]*x**q*np.log(x) + np.cos(w*t)*params[0]*0 + params[7]*0 
            + params[8]*0 + 0*r)
